subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off successful `memoryFlush.resetAfterFlush` mode, and should that policy be unified with reset-time memory preservation from #45608?
rationale: The remaining work changes session lifecycle, model/provider routing for private transcript handling, and data-retention semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary.

options.title: Design one reset-memory policy first
options.body: Define a single default-off policy covering compaction-threshold reset-after-flush plus `/new`, `/reset`, and daily reset memory preservation before implementation.

options.title: Approve narrow reset-after-flush
options.body: Implement only the compaction-threshold successful flush-then-reset mode with strict timeout, provider, audit, notification, and tests/proof requirements.

options.title: Reject automatic reset-after-flush
options.body: Keep the shipped model override surfaces and require ordinary compaction, manual reset, or separately approved reset-time memory preservation instead.

recommendation.title: Design one reset-memory policy first
recommendation.body: Define a single default-off policy covering compaction-threshold reset-after-flush plus `/new`, `/reset`, and daily reset memory preservation before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the central pre-compaction memory flush path and memory-flush model override, so they are the best available history owner for the remaining lifecycle decision.
